transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. From what you have described, the most likely cause is sump / tub-to-pump hose. Next: Establish WHERE the water appears, WHEN in the cycle, and what it LOOKS like before choosing a part. Let me know what you find.

ok the water's coming from the front of the machine, it started mid-wash today. I'm standing in socks on the wet floor right now and the water has run back towards the socket. The fuse box is in the hall where the floor is dry, so should I go and switch it off there now?

Yes, switch it off at the fuse box in the hall now, and don't touch the plug, socket or machine while you're standing on the wet floor. Put on dry shoes before you walk back into the kitchen, and leave the power off until the floor around the socket is dry. From what you have described, the most likely cause is door seal. Front leaks are most often the rubber door seal. Open the door and look all the way round the seal, including inside the folds at the bottom — a trapped coin, underwire or sock can hold it open, and splits often hide in the folds. Is the seal intact, did you find something trapped in it, or is it torn or split?
ok I've switched it off at the fuse box. I looked at the door seal and there's a small split in the bottom fold of the rubber, and a bra underwire stuck right next to it. Is that what's causing it??

Yes, very likely: a split in the bottom fold of the door seal lets water escape from the front during a wash, and the stuck underwire is a common cause of that kind of tear. Before anything else, with water reaching the socket and you in socks on a wet floor, don't touch the plug or the machine; turn the power off at the consumer unit (fuse box) while standing on dry ground. Next: If the door seal is ripped, check the drum for up/down play, a dropped drum or bearing noise so a replacement seal isn't destroyed too. Let me know what you find.
I'm not sure how to check the drum for play, I wouldn't know what I was feeling for. It sounded normal while it was washing though. Can I just get a new seal, or do I need someone in?

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Before anything else: water has reached the socket while the machine is running, so don't touch the plug, socket or machine while standing on the wet floor in socks, and if you can reach your fuse box from dry ground, switch that circuit off there. As for the seal, you can usually buy one and fit it yourself if you're reasonably handy, as it's held on by two clamp bands, though it's a fiddly job The checks point to the door seal. To find the right part, could you give me the model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
